=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:81-90 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The push-URL test expects hide to reject a credential-bearing `remote.origin.pushurl`, but the helper does not inspect that setting and returns success.
  WHY: The test fails while the credential-bearing push URL remains configured during editor execution.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:76-92 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore accepts any `https://github.com/` origin without verifying it matches the trusted repository identity, then injects `GH_TOKEN`.
  WHY: An editor-changed origin such as `https://github.com/attacker/repo.git` passes the host check and receives the workflow token.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:19-92 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Hide and restore do not inspect or reject `remote.origin.pushurl` or `url.*.pushInsteadOf`.
  WHY: Push destinations can bypass the sanitized origin and retain credentials or redirect pushes to an attacker-controlled destination.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:85-93 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore reinstates a generic GitHub `extraheader` instead of scoping it to the verified repository endpoint.
  WHY: The generic header sends credentials with any request to github.com rather than only to the trusted repository.
- tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:40-41 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The test expects restoration to create a repository-scoped extraheader and remove the generic header, but the helper restores the original generic key.
  WHY: The scoped-key lookup fails because the helper restores the header at the generic key.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:61-97 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore injects credentials into checkouts sequentially instead of validating every checkout first.
  WHY: If a later checkout fails validation, an earlier checkout has already received the token.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:21-102 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Hide and restore return success when safety-critical operations fail, including marker errors, credential-removal failures, missing `GH_TOKEN`, and restoration failures.
  WHY: Callers proceed as though credentials were safely hidden or restored; the highest severity is critical, though one reviewer classified a subset of these failures as major.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:25-52 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Hide does not verify that `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` is present and valid before hiding credentials.
  WHY: The expected trusted-repository identity check cannot function reliably without that validation.
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:38 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The workspace path filter rejects paths containing “credential,” including `scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh`.
  WHY: The review editor cannot transfer changes to that script, preventing autonomous fixes to the credential-isolation defects.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:2103-2105, 2437-2439, 2874-2889, 2892-2894, 4146-4160 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]

  WHY: The editor can read untrusted job-log slices from that directory despite the structured-diagnostics-only prompt boundary; one reviewer classified this as major and the other as blocker.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py: lines 81-90, function test_hide_rejects_an_explicit_push_url_before_editor_launch | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The last run added this test, which expects hide to return nonzero when remote.origin.pushurl points to an attacker-controlled repository. However, scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh has zero code to inspect pushurl, pushInsteadOf, or any push-writing configuration. The hide action only reads and sanitizes remote.origin.url (lines 35-36) and removes http.*.extraheader config entries (lines 45-53). A grep for pushurl|push.url|pushInsteadOf in that file returns no matches. The helper will successfully sanitize the origin URL, skip the uninspected pushurl entirely, and exit 0 -- but the test asserts returncode != 0.
  WHY: When this test runs in CI, the second hide call produces exit code 0 from the helper (which sees only the clean origin URL), and the assertion assert result.returncode != 0 fails, breaking CI.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 81-83 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The origin restoration check matches any repository under https://github.com/ rather than verifying that the repository matches the trusted repository identity from GITHUB_REPOSITORY or the verified support repository.
  WHY: If an editor process modifies .git/config so origin points to an attacker repository on GitHub (e.g., https://github.com/attacker/repo.git), the restore action injects the workflow GH_TOKEN into that URL. This violates the trust boundary and causes tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:51-65 (test_restore_does_not_send_token_to_an_editor_changed_origin) to fail.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 34-44 and lines 77-84 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Neither hide nor restore inspects or sanitizes remote.origin.pushurl or url.<base>.pushInsteadOf.
  WHY: A pre-existing or editor-injected push URL remains active in .git/config during editor execution and after restoration. Git pushes bypass the sanitized origin URL and target the push URL instead, exposing tokens or redirecting pushed code. tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:81-91 (test_hide_rejects_an_explicit_push_url_before_editor_launch), lines 68-78 (test_restore_rejects_editor_changed_push_url), and lines 93-104 (test_restore_rejects_editor_changed_push_url_rewrite) all fail as a result.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 85-93 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The restore action restores the generic http.https://github.com/.extraheader config key instead of scoping the authorization header to the verified repository endpoint.
  WHY: Restoring a root-scoped extraheader broadcasts credentials to any request sent to github.com. tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:40-41 expects the header scoped to http.https://github.com/owner/repo.git.extraheader and asserts the generic key is absent, while lines 130-140 (test_restore_rejects_untrusted_extraheader_scope) asserts rejection of untrusted scopes; both fail against the current script.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 62-97 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The restore loop applies credential updates to checkouts sequentially before validating all checkouts listed in the marker file.
  WHY: If the primary repository is processed first and a subsequent support checkout (.codex-workflow-src) fails validation due to a modified remote, the primary repository is left in a credentialed state despite overall restore failure. tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:155-171 (test_restore_validates_every_checkout_before_injecting_any_token) asserts that validation must succeed across all repositories before any token injection occurs.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 21-27, lines 57-60, and line 102 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The script exits with status 0 on error paths, including when an unrestored marker already exists (line 23), when marker creation fails (line 27), when GH_TOKEN is unset during restore (line 59), and after restore encounters failures (line 102).
  WHY: Unconditional exit 0 prevents workflow callers from detecting failures and failing closed. It also causes multiple contract tests in tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py (e.g., lines 46-47 for missing tokens, lines 112-113 for existing markers, and lines 59-60 for invalid origins) that assert non-zero return codes to fail.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 29-33 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The hide action does not verify that GITHUB_REPOSITORY is present and valid before hiding credentials.
  WHY: Without validating GITHUB_REPOSITORY, subsequent repository identity checks cannot function reliably. tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:143-152 (test_hide_fails_without_trusted_repository_identity) expects hide to exit with a non-zero status when GITHUB_REPOSITORY is missing.
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py: line 38 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The path filter in scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:38 rejects any file whose name contains "credential", causing allowed("scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh") to return False.
  WHY: Review autofix runs inside a container managed by review_untrusted_workspace.py. When the review editor attempts to modify scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh to resolve security findings, transfer_changes fails with ValueError("unsafe result path") and discards the changes. This creates a wedged review autofix cycle where the editor repeatedly reports fixing the script, but the changes cannot transfer to the host git tree. The script should be renamed (e.g., scripts/editor_git_auth.sh) to avoid matching the credential-filter keyword.
